title: Ethiopia Opens Up: Ethio Telecom's IPO, the Birr Float and the Debt Deal | The Six, Ep. 15
lede: In five years Ethiopia has sold a telecom licence to a Safaricom-led group, floated the birr, opened the Ethiopian Securities Exchange and sold shares in Ethio Telecom to 47,377 investors. The birr has lost almost two-thirds of its value against the dollar since the July 2024 float, and a deal with Eurobond holders, cleared by official creditors in August, is awaiting final documents.
keyPoints: Ethio Telecom offered 100 million shares (10%) at 300 birr; 47,377 investors bought about 10.7 million, raising about 3.2 billion birr ($24.5 million) against a $240 million hope. The shares began trading on the ESX on May 26, 2026 (The Reporter; CIO Africa; Semafor).

The Ethiopian Securities Exchange, opened Jan. 10, 2025, lists seven companies, six of them banks; nine more are approved to list and the target is 15 by June 2027 (BusinessDay; The Reporter Ethiopia).

Safaricom's consortium paid $850 million for a licence in May 2021 and passed 15 million active customers in September 2026; Ethio Telecom reported 90.1 million customers and 60.59 million telebirr users for FY2025/26 (Al Jazeera; Safaricom Ethiopia; ENA).
The birr went from 57.48 per dollar before the July 29, 2024 float to a 159.19 cut-off at the central bank's Nov. 10, 2026 auction (Addis Insight; Capital Ethiopia).

Ethiopia defaulted on its $1 billion Eurobond in December 2023; bondholders agreed a 12% haircut on June 29, 2026, and official creditors cleared it in August. The IMF has paid out about $2.65 billion of a $3.4 billion programme (Ecofin; Ministry of Finance; IMF).
